title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles were not designed to operate for extended periods in stationary traffic, and at least a dozen of them became stranded on San Francisco streets when their batteries depleted during Fourth of July celebrations. The vehicles encountered unplanned road closures and unexpected congestion that trapped them without charging options. A human fleet operator monitoring traffic conditions in real time, or geofencing that prevented vehicles from entering areas with uncertain egress during major events, could have prevented the stranding.

The incident reveals a gap between the conditions autonomous vehicles are tested in and conditions that occur during major public events with unpredictable traffic patterns and road closures. It is not established whether Waymo's routing system had access to information about the fireworks or road closures ahead of time, or what alerts or manual override options were available to fleet operators to redirect vehicles before they became trapped.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets on Saturday during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while trapped in heavy traffic. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following fireworks from the Golden Gate Bridge. Some vehicles required towing to clear the roadways. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion.

The incident highlighted challenges for autonomous vehicles during major events. One passenger reported a Waymo continued driving despite fireworks being set off in the street, and a vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks with no injuries reported. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office indicated plans to discuss the traffic situation with public and private partners. This marks the second significant issue for Waymo in San Francisco, following a December outage when vehicles stopped at intersections with nonworking traffic lights during a power failure affecting over 100,000 customers.
